proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, 3^n is congruent to 3^(n mod 3) modulo 13.

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n*(n+1) is at least 2*n.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^3 > 20.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^2 > 40.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, if n mod 3 = 0 then 3^(n) mod 13 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-3)*(2*n) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 46 modulo 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-4)*(n^2) equals (n-4)*((n^2) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 37, 3^(n+3) mod 13 is congruent to 3^(n) mod 13 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 2185 modulo 115.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n*(n+1) is at least 2*n.
The steps above establish the statement up to 40, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 40.
